reason: The cited evidence supports the existence of fast cooling rates and a nucleation-condensation mechanism for ultrasmall NPs, but it does not demonstrate that varying laser parameters (pulse duration, energy density) controls phase homogeneity or catalytic performance, nor does it address noble metal–based HEAs. The key premises about kinetic trapping of a homogeneous phase and its catalytic superiority are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Ultrafast laser ablation can kinetically trap homogeneous single-phase HEA nanoparticles by limiting atomic diffusion
Lower energy density and shorter pulse duration reduce post-nucleation atomic mobility
Homogeneous single-phase HEA nanoparticles with isolated noble metal sites exhibit superior catalytic performance
Higher energy or longer pulses cause phase segregation due to increased atomic mobility
Cooling rates during laser ablation are sufficiently high (~10^12 K/s) to suppress phase separation
